# 1 Clement 60 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 1 Clement 60 (4 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Total disagreements logged:** 5

---

## V.1 — "everlasting constitution" / "everlasting fabric" / "eternal order"
- **EMET:** "everlasting constitution" / **LOGOS:** "everlasting fabric" / **PNEUMA:** "eternal order"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Everlasting constitution" (EMET) — the Greek *aiōnion systasis* means an ordered, established structure. "Constitution" preserves the sense of a divinely ordered system. "Fabric" (LOGOS) leans toward the material/woven metaphor; "order" (PNEUMA) is too generic.

---

## V.1 — "wonderful in strength and splendor" / "wonderful in power and majesty"
- **EMET:** "wonderful in strength and splendor" / **LOGOS:** "wonderful in power and majesty" / **PNEUMA:** "wonderful in your power and majesty"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Wonderful in power and majesty" (LOGOS) — the Greek *ischyi kai megaloprepeia* = power and magnificence/majesty. "Majesty" is the better rendering for *megaloprepeia* (greatness of bearing/magnificence).

---

## V.2 — "cleanse us with the cleansing of your truth" / "purify us with the purification of your truth"
- **EMET:** "cleanse us with the cleansing of your truth" / **LOGOS:** "purify us with the purification of your truth" / **PNEUMA:** "purify us with the cleansing of your truth"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Cleanse us with the cleansing of your truth" (EMET) — the doubled root (*katharismō... katharari*) in Greek creates an emphatic figure. "Cleanse" / "cleansing" preserves the figured speech. "Purify/purification" (LOGOS) is synonymous but loses the alliterative figure.

---

## V.3 — "protect us" / "be our shelter" / "be our shelter"
- **EMET:** "protect us" / **LOGOS:** "be our shelter" / **PNEUMA:** "be our shelter"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Protect us" — the Greek *skopesei* means "will watch over/guard." "Protect" (EMET) is clean and accurate. "Shelter" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) adds a spatial metaphor not in the Greek.

---

## V.4 — "all-powerful and all-excellent name" / "all-powerful and most excellent name"
- **EMET:** "omnipotent and all-excellent name" / **LOGOS:** "all-powerful and most excellent name" / **PNEUMA:** "all-powerful and glorious name"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "All-powerful and most excellent name" (LOGOS) — "omnipotent" (EMET) is a Latin-derived theological term; "all-powerful" is the Greek equivalent (*pantokratori*). "Most excellent" is better than "all-excellent" for *megaloprepestatos*.

---

*— SOPHIA*
